text:
incident-bot: :warning: Alert: Sudden spike in 502/504 errors observed at API gateway. 5xx rate crossed 4% in us-west-2 at 14:03 UTC. Paging oncall (maya) and platform.

maya: oncall here, joining. what's the initial signal? graphs?

trent: Grafana shows a sharp jump in gateway 502/504 between 14:01-14:05 UTC. Ingress CPU fine, but upstream TLS errors in edge-proxy logs: 
```
[14:02:17] error tls: handshake failure from model-router-1: TLS alert: handshake_failure
[14:02:18] error upstream: connection reset by peer
```

rebecca: curious — we rotated certs on the model-router cluster as part of midnight maintenance, but that was hours ago. Any cert expiry events?

oscar: checking cert status... model-router cert renewed at 02:01 UTC and appears valid. However, I see a flood of ephemeral-port exhaustion on model-router hosts around 14:00: many sockets stuck in TIME_WAIT. netstat shows ephemeral ports consumed ~60k (limit 65k).

devops-bot: automated note: model-router autoscaler spun up new pods at 13:58 but kube-proxy shows large NAT table churn.

maya: hypothesis: rapid scale-up + short TCP TIME_WAIT + TLS renegotiations = ephemeral port exhaustion leading to upstream resets which manifest as 502/504 at gateway. Could explain regional spike if a subset of hosts hit NAT limits.

trent: adding quick probe: curl small health endpoint through edge to model-router pool with verbose to capture TLS handshake. Result: repeated 'no available ports' and 'connection reset' on some backend hosts.

rebecca: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) enable conn reuse/keepalive on edge to reduce new ephemeral port usage, 2) reduce TLS renegotiation (disable client-side renegotiation), 3) increase ephemeral port range on model-router nodes, 4) if possible, shift small percentage of traffic to standby pool in another AZ.

maya: agreed. I'm going to toggle keepalive on edge-proxy to ON for model-router connections and roll to a small canary set.

devops-bot: canary config applied to edge-proxy-a and -b (us-west-2a).

trent: i'm patching kube nodes to widen ephemeral port range and reduce TIME_WAIT timeout on two model-router hosts (canary):
```
echo 1024 65535 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30
```
Applying via ssh to mr-node-07 and mr-node-09.

oscar: applied sysctl changes to canary hosts. ephemeral ports available increased; monitoring shows immediate drop in connect errors for those hosts.

maya: routing: shifting 20% of ambiguous traffic to standby model-router pool in us-west-2b. Implementing weighted routing in traffic-router.

devops-bot: weighted routing applied: standby pool receives 20% traffic.

trent: after keepalive and sysctl changes, 5xx rate dropped from 4.3% -> 1.7% in 3 minutes. TIME_WAIT counts on canary hosts declined. Remaining hosts still high; plan to roll sysctl change across all model-router nodes gradually.

rebecca: I'm opening a maintenance runway: rolling apply ephemeral port expansion + tcp_fin_timeout change cluster-wide with 30s stagger to avoid burst. Also adding a short-lived hairpin to avoid external NAT exhaustion.

support-bot: quick customer-impact check: Support dashboard shows 9% failure rate for a small cohort of customers in us-west-2 at peak; 11 customers flagged, 2 reported errors to support. Sending templated notice: "We're investigating elevated 5xx on generation endpoints in US West; mitigation in progress."

oscar: note: TLS handshake failures also show mismatched cipher list during some reconnections — older clients on model-router may be falling back to weaker ciphers causing renegotiation churn. I'll pin cipher list to a common subset during rollout.

maya: good call. rebecca, include cipher pin in the rollout template. Also add alert for ephemeral port utilization exceeding 80% for any host.

rebecca: alert added: net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range usage >80% -> pager. Runbook updated at https://go/repo/ops/runbooks/ephemeral-port-exhaustion.

trent: rolling sysctl changes to all 12 model-router worker nodes now. ETA 6 minutes.

maya: monitoring: 5xx now 0.9% globally; us-west-2 at 0.6%. Good trend. Keep an eye for regression when we remove weighted routing.

oscar: full cluster changes applied. No new TLS handshakes errors observed. NAT table churn reduced.

support-bot: customer notifications: initial message delivered to flagged customers. Follow-up note prepared for postmortem.

maya: root-cause (interim): rapid scaling + cert/cipher mismatch + aggressive TLS renegotiation patterns caused many short-lived connections, which combined with default ephemeral port limits caused port exhaustion on model-router hosts. This led to upstream resets and gateway 502/504 for a subset of requests.

rebecca: follow-ups: 1) make ephemeral port range change part of node baseline, 2) add preflight check to kube autoscaler to limit simultaneous pod churn per host, 3) implement connection reuse improvements in edge-proxy, 4) add cipher alignment check in deploy pipeline, 5) add alert for socket/TIME_WAIT anomalies.

maya: handoff: i'll remain oncall for 20 minutes to confirm stability. If anything flares, page oncall-next (oscar). Postmortem owner: rebecca.

devops-bot: incident mitigated at 14:19 UTC. Automated severity: S3.

maya: thanks all. please attach graphs (TIME_WAIT, ephemeral ports, 5xx timeline) to the postmortem and include the exact sysctl and routing commands used.

trent: copying commands used for reference:
```
# expand ephemeral ports and shorten TIME_WAIT
for h in $(cat mr-nodes.txt); do ssh $h "sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='1024 65535'; sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30"; done

# enable keepalive on edge-proxy for model-router upstream
kubectl patch configmap edge-proxy-config -n edge --patch '{"data":{"upstream_keepalive":"on"}}'

# apply weighted routing
curl -XPATCH "https://traffic-router/api/v1/routes/weight" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","weights":{"primary":80,"standby":20}}'
```

support-bot: post-incident follow-up: support will send a consolidated customer update once postmortem is drafted.

maya: closing mitigation channel. final status: stabilized, us-west-2 5xx <1% after ops. Postmortem assigned to rebecca, follow-ups to devops and edge teams. Good work. :thumbsup:
